target_period: Mulga1 2010-2023 and Mulga2 2024-2026 are separate files; dieback 2018-2020 not represented
rationale: v1.1 (2 Nov 2026): woody 65 = airborne-lidar canopy cover (pixels >2 m, 5x5 km; Fischer et al. 2024), the lowest of three crown-cover estimates (74.5 % of land area, Cleverly et al. 2016 AFM 220:151 Sect. 2.1; TERN core plot 70-80 %); v1 woody 43 came from an LAI ratio. The remaining 35 is split herb 18 % / bare 82 % from TERN AusPlots point-intercept points without a woody hit (NTABRT0001/0002 next to the tower, 1,010 points, Mar 2012 wet and Jul-Aug 2020 dry; herb share 7-27 %, mean 18 %). Herb C3:C4 = 35:65, the mean of the four visits (2012 C3 ~68 % of grass, mainly Thyridolepis mitchelliana; 2020 C4 ~99 %, Paspalidium, Aristida). Mulga stays FATES4 as decided in OzFlux Stage21.
residual_policy: Herbs under the mulga canopy cannot be represented with nocomp patches and are omitted; the herb share counts only open-ground points, which may under-estimate open-interspace grass.
bare_policy: Bare 29 = 0.82 x (100 - 65). AusPlots points with no plant hit are 37-49 % of all points; their substrate is about 30-50 % bare soil, 25-45 % litter and 24-32 % cryptogam crust. The FATES bare share therefore includes litter and crust.
nonvascular_policy: Cryptogam crust (15-20 % of substrate points) is inside the bare share; not a FATES PFT.
source_composition: Acacia aneura + A. aptaneura; C3 forbs/shrubs; C3 perennial grass; C4 perennial and annual grasses (L6 vegetation1-4)
source_denominator: Crown cover: lidar 65 % of CHM pixels >2 m (preprint); 74.5 % of land area (method not stated); TERN core plot 70-80 %. AusPlots 1,010-point intercept: woody hit 37-56 %, herb hit 13-31 %, no plant hit 37-49 %.
hold_flag: Woody 65 (lidar) vs 74.5 (Cleverly 2016) kept as sensitivity; herb density in open interspaces assumed equal to crown gaps; FATES4 vs FATES7 per Stage21-22

target_state: Post-clearcut state (operator decision 2 Nov 2026): hybrid larch strips plus retained Sasa strips

rationale: v1.1 (2 Nov 2026): after the Jan-Mar 2003 clear-cut the Sasa was strip-cut in 4 m rows and ~2500/ha hybrid larch (Larix gmelinii x kaempferi) were planted in the cut rows in Oct 2003; cut and uncut rows each cover half of the area (Aguilos et al. 2014 Sect. 3.2; AsiaFlux TSE; Tsunogai et al. 2014 Sect. 2.1). This planting design is an area measurement: larch rows -> DNF 50, Sasa rows -> CoolC3 50 (Sasa senanensis/kurilensis, evergreen dwarf bamboo).
residual_policy: Sasa re-invaded the larch rows after weeding stopped (2007) and covered the gaps between trees by 2008-2010; nocomp patches keep the 50/50 area split and drop the Sasa under larch. Natural Betula/Quercus regeneration is unquantified. Seasonal-mean PAI: larch 0.9 (2004) -> 1.7 (2013), Sasa 4.3-6.1 (Sun et al. 2020 Table 1).
bare_policy: Bare 0 from 2007; the larch rows were weeded in 2004-2006 and were partly bare then (sensitivity weeded_strips_2004_2006).
source_composition: Hybrid larch ~2500/ha planted Oct 2003 in 4 m strip-cut rows; Sasa in the alternate uncut rows; natural Betula ermanii, B. platyphylla, Quercus crispula. Pre-cut: Q. crispula, Betula, Abies sachalinensis, Picea jezoensis.
source_denominator: Planting design: strip-cut and uncut rows each half of the study area; PAI by year (Sun et al. 2020 Table 1).
hold_flag: Sasa is approximated as cool C3 grass; pre-2003 forest years not represented
next_evidence: Larch height and canopy closure after 2010; birch share; JapanFlux BADM vegetation file.

target_state: Windthrown former larch plantation in natural regrowth; compromise between the C3-herb state (2010-2014) and the birch state (after ~2015)
rationale: v1.1 (2 Nov 2026): Typhoon Songda (8 Sep 2004) blew down >90 % of the trees; trunks were salvage-logged by summer 2005, stumps and branches left, no replanting, no larch survived (Sano et al. 2010 Sect. 2.1; Yazaki et al. 2016 Sect. 2.1, 3.1). Understorey: Rubus idaeus ~60 % of biomass and ~50 % of LAI in 2006, >60 % of biomass to 2009; Solidago gigantea ~70 % of understorey biomass in 2011. Birch (B. platyphylla, B. ermanii): overstorey LAI 0.40 (2010) and 0.76 (2014) against understorey LAI 2.7-3.6; trees 48 % of aboveground biomass in 2014; Betula-dominated by ~2019-2022 (qualitative). The primary is the mid state shifted toward trees; period scenarios give each state.
residual_policy: LAI and biomass shares are used as area proxies; no area or cover fraction exists for any year. All understorey species are C3 (Rubus, Solidago, Dryopteris, Pachysandra); no Sasa at this site.
bare_policy: Bare 5 is a placeholder for stump pits, coarse woody debris and machine-disturbed soil; the 2006 understorey LAI ~3.8 implies a nearly closed low canopy.
source_composition: Rubus idaeus (deciduous shrub) 2005-2009, Solidago gigantea (C3 forb) 2010-2014, Betula platyphylla and B. ermanii saplings rising to dominance; larch 67/ha in 2014.
source_denominator: Yazaki et al. 2016 Table 1, Table A1, Sect. 3.1-3.3; Sano et al. 2010 Sect. 3.1; qualitative 2019-2022 statements.
hold_flag: Dominant PFT changes twice within the record; nothing quantitative after 2014; a scraped bare-pumice patch ~0.2 km north may or may not be in the footprint
next_evidence: Yazaki 2016 Tables S5-S6; Hirano et al. 2017 AFM 232:457; JapanFlux BADM vegetation files.
